bug_description.original: Heap-use-after-free in XInclude processing: xmlXIncludeLoadTxt (xinclude.c) can end up calling xmlStaticCopyNode (tree.c) on a node that has already been freed (by the XML reader code), resulting in a read of freed heap memory. An attacker-controlled XML with XInclude can trigger this, causing crashes, memory corruption, or potentially enabling information disclosure or further exploitation.
bug_description.normalized: Repeated XInclude text includes with the same resolved href let libxml2 cache an `xmlNodePtr` in `xmlXIncludeCtxt->txtTab`. The saved ASan artifacts prove that a node allocated by `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt` is later freed along the reader cleanup path `xmlTextReaderRead -> xmlTextReaderFreeNode -> xmlTextReaderFreeNodeList`, while `txtTab` still retains the stale pointer. When a later `parse="text"` include hits the same URL cache entry, `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt` reuses that dangling pointer in `xmlCopyNode`, and `xmlStaticCopyNode` reads freed heap memory.

source.description: The project first reads the attacker-controlled include attributes that matter for this path here: `href` becomes the later cache key after URI resolution and `parse` selects the text-loading branch.

sink.description: `xmlCopyNode` forwards the cached pointer into `xmlStaticCopyNode`, which immediately reads `node->type`; the saved ASan trace reports this read as the heap-use-after-free sink.

root_cause.description: The XInclude text cache stores the original `xmlNodePtr` instead of an owned copy of the text payload, so any later reader-side reclamation of that node leaves a dangling pointer in `ctxt->txtTab`.

coarse_trace.summary: The streaming reader encounters an XInclude element from the attacker XML and invokes XInclude processing on that parsed node.
XInclude reads the attacker-controlled `href` and `parse` attributes, resolves the URL, and dispatches `parse="text"` includes into `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt`.
The first text include for that resolved URL loads external text into a newly allocated text node and caches the node pointer in `ctxt->txtTab`.
Later reader cleanup frees a node through the ASan-reported reader reclamation path, while the XInclude cache still retains the stale pointer.
A later text include resolving to the same URL hits the cache and passes the stale pointer into `xmlCopyNode`.
`xmlStaticCopyNode` dereferences the freed node pointer, producing the observed ASan heap-use-after-free read.

fine_trace.code:
if ((reader->xinclude) && (reader->node != NULL) &&
    (reader->node->type == XML_ELEMENT_NODE) &&
    (reader->node->ns != NULL) &&
    ((xmlStrEqual(reader->node->ns->href, XINCLUDE_NS)) ||
     (xmlStrEqual(reader->node->ns->href, XINCLUDE_OLD_NS)))) { ... xmlXIncludeProcessNode(reader->xincctxt, reader->node); }
fine_trace.note: While streaming the witness XML, the reader reaches an element in the XInclude namespace and calls `xmlXIncludeProcessNode` on that parsed include node.

fine_trace.code:
if ((xmlStrEqual(node->ns->href, XINCLUDE_NS)) ||
    (xmlStrEqual(node->ns->href, XINCLUDE_OLD_NS))) { ... if (xmlStrEqual(node->name, XINCLUDE_NODE)) { ... return(1); } }
fine_trace.note: XInclude processing admits this parsed element as an `<include>` node in the XInclude namespace, enabling preprocessing and include loading.

Source. The include node's attacker-controlled `href` and `parse` attributes are read here; `parse="text"` converts to `xml = 0`, selecting the text-loading path, and `href` is the input later resolved into the cache key.
libxml2 resolves the attacker-provided `href` into the canonical `URI` string later compared against `ctxt->txturlTab[i]` for cache hits.
For the first `parse="text"` include of this resolved `URI`, libxml2 allocates a text node, fills it with the loaded external text, and passes that live node into the XInclude text cache.

Root-cause step. The cache stores the original text-node pointer together with a copied URL string; it does not duplicate the text payload, so the cache entry becomes stale if reader-side code later reclaims that node object.

The saved ASan free stack proves that a later reader advance reaches `xmlTextReaderFreeNode` from `xmlTextReaderRead` line 1504. This is the caller-side entry into the reader reclamation path that invalidates a node later reused from the XInclude cache, even though the saved artifacts do not identify the precise caller-side alias beyond this stack frame.

On a later include with the same resolved `URL`, the cache-hit path reuses `ctxt->txtTab[i]` without any validity check. The saved ASan evidence shows the reused pointer has already been freed somewhere along the reader cleanup path, so `xmlCopyNode` now receives a dangling pointer.
Sink. `xmlCopyNode` forwards the stale cached pointer into `xmlStaticCopyNode`, which immediately reads `node->type`; the saved ASan report identifies this read as the heap-use-after-free crash.

format.name: XML with repeated XInclude text includes
format.contract: The witnessed trigger is the saved XML structure with repeated XInclude `include` elements in the XInclude namespace, each carrying `parse="text"` and the same resolved `href` (`../ents/isolatin.txt` in the saved testcase), so `xmlXIncludeLoadTxt` first stores an `xmlNodePtr` in `ctxt->txtTab` for that URL and a later matching include reuses the same cached entry by URL. The saved artifacts do not statically prove which reader-side alias reaches the free site, only that reader cleanup frees a node on the ASan-reported path before that cached pointer is reused.
